sentences.text:
Aggrieved by Annexure-1 judgment passed in C.C.No.55/2014, on the file of the Court of the Special Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Thrissur, convicting the petitioners and sentencing the 1 st petitioner to pay a fine of Rs.1,08,000/- and the petitioners 2 to 5 to undergo simple imprisonment Tik Innovators Marketing Ltd vs State Of Kerala on 7 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/134042829/
2 for a period of one year and also to pay a fine, the petitioners have preferred Crl.A.No.261/2025 before the Court of Session, Thrissur (Appellate Court).

entities.text: Special Additional Chief Judicial Magistrate, Thrissur
entities.label: COURT

entities.text: Tik Innovators Marketing Ltd vs State Of Kerala
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Along with the appeal, the petitioners also filed Annexure-3 application to suspend the substantive sentence and sentence of fine.
2. By the impugned Annexure 4 order, the Appellate Court has conditionally suspended the sentence by directing the petitioners to remit 20% of the fine amount within one month.
The impugned direction is onerous and unjustifiable.

There is no provision in the Bharatiya Nagarik Suraksha Sanhita, 2023 ('BNSS', in short) that mandates the accused CRL.MC NO. 10033 OF 2025 2025:KER:84553 persons to deposit the fine/compensation amount for the purpose of suspending the sentence, unlike an offence under Section 138 of the Negotiable Instruments Act, 1881.
The petitioners have raised valid grounds in the appeal and are advised that there is every likelihood of the appeal being allowed in their favour.

The condition to deposit the fine amount is unwarranted,
and therefore, may be set aside.
3. I have heard the learned Counsel for the petitioners and the learned Public Prosecutor.

4. Indisputably, the petitioners have been convicted for having allegedly committed the offences punishable under Sections 406 and 420 read with Section 34 of the Indian Penal Code and Sections 3, 4 5 and 6 of the of the Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978.

entities.text: Prize Chits and Money Circulation Schemes (Banning) Act, 1978
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: 5. The learned Sessions Judge, on considering the nature, gravity and financial implications of the offences, has directed the petitioners to deposit 20% of the total fine amount within one month.

Going by the provisions under the BNSS, I do not find that there is any mandatory stipulation that 20% of the fine amount has to be deposited unlike Section CRL.MC NO. 10033 OF 2025 2025:KER:84553 148 of the N.I.Act, especially in a statutory appeal filed before the Appellate Court under Section 415 (3) of the BNSS.
However, it is the discretion of the Appellate Court to impose such conditions as it may deem fit.

6. Recently, in Central Bureau of Investigation v. Ashok Sirpal (2024 KHC 6592), the Honourable Supreme Court has held that conditions that defeat the right of an appellant-accused to be enlarged on bail shall be avoided because it violates his fundamental right under Article 21 of the Constitution of India.

entities.text: Central Bureau of Investigation v. Ashok Sirpal (2024 KHC 6592)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Therefore, I am of the definite view that the condition in Annexure-4 order, directing the petitioners to deposit 20% of the fine amount, is onerous.
In the aforesaid circumstance, I allow the Crl.M.C. by setting aside the condition in Annexure-4 order, directing the petitioners to deposit 20% of the fine amount within one month.
However, the petitioners shall execute the bond for Rs.1/- lakh with two solvent sureties as directed in Annexure-4 order.
